Priya / Ben — thanks for the loop. I reviewed MedSyn's redline (attached Legal_Commentary_Sept7.pdf) and here are the discrete positions and recommended concessions: 

1) SCCs / Transfer Addendum:
- We can accept EU Commission SCCs as the baseline. For the Transfer Impact Addendum, we prefer Redwood's standard wording which documents technical and organisational measures (TOMs) and references the SCCs; MedSyn's proposed TI addendum adds a requirement for per-export evidence (sample logs) that is operationally heavy. Consider a compromise: accept the SCCs + add a short clause committing to provide "export routing summary and redacted proof-of-export" on request (not automatic delivery).

2) Roles (Controller / Processor):
- Confirm Redwood is Processor. We will not accept language that reclassifies Redwood as a joint controller. We'll add explicit processor-only language and a short schedule enumerating processing activities.

3) Subprocessors / notification window:
- 30-day prior approval is high friction. Our standard is 30-day notification with an exception for critical infra providers where we provide notice "as soon as practicable". Proposed redline: limited list for named subprocessors + 30-day notice for new non-critical subprocessors; a 10-business-day notice for urgent security fixes.

4) Audit / Evidence requests:
- SOC2 report share: acceptable on NDA. Live access to logs or on-site audit: push back. Offer a SOC2 + summary export logs for the last 90 days redacted. If they insist on live access, we require mutual NDA & pre-scheduled scope.

5) Deletion / Retention SLA and export deletion on termination:
- Accept standard deletion language; we will require a short exception window for backups (30 days). If they require immediate purge from backups, this will need an operational change and additional commercial consideration.

Commercial consideration: if procurement demands narrow subprocessor approvals or per-export logs, recommend we offer a one-time professional services credit (suggest $15k) to cover the extra operations work and accelerate signature. Ben, please confirm whether commercial is aligned.

Proposed next step: Priya to send consolidated redline (SCCs + our proposed compromise language) to Alicia by Thu 9 Sep. If MedSyn remains firm on immediate access to logs or 30-day prior approval for all subprocessors, escalate for exec approval.

Laura Bennett

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the redline and for outlining procurement timing. After internal review we've consolidated Redwood's positions and a proposed path forward below. Please treat this as Redwood's formal response to the attached MedSyn DPA redline.

Summary of Redwood positions (high-level):
- Roles: Redwood accepts Processor designation; we will provide a short schedule of processing activities.
- SCCs: We can adopt the EU Commission SCCs as the baseline; we propose the attached DPA with SCC insertion + a limited Transfer Impact clause that references our TOMs and commits to supply a redacted export summary on request.
- Subprocessors: We will provide a current named subprocessor list and 30-day notification for new non-critical subprocessors. For critical infra (hosting, KMS, observability) we reserve the right to add with "as soon as practicable" notice; emergency patches will have a 10-business-day post-notification window.
- Audit / Evidence: We will provide the most recent SOC2 Type II report under NDA and will provide redacted export summaries (sample logs) upon reasonable request. Live log access or on-site audits require an NDA and pre-scoped engagement.
- Retention / Deletion: Standard deletion with a 30-day backup exception.

Commercial ask: if MedSyn requires per-export logs by default or strict prior approval for all subprocessors, this increases operational burden. We'd propose a one-time professional services credit of $15,000 to cover implementation of additional reporting and expedited legal review. Ben, confirm if that remains our internal proposal.

Proposed timeline:
- Deliver consolidated DPA markup (Docx + PDF) to MedSyn: Thu 9 Sep (EOD).
- Optional 30 min call to review consolidated positions: Fri 10 Sep 14:00 - 14:30 GMT (please confirm availability).
- Target: Order Form + DPA in DocuSign by Mon 13 Sep; final signature by 20 Sep per procurement ask.

DocuSign: We'll prepare an envelope and share after you confirm the combined DPA/Order Form approach. Link will be shared and I will copy procurement.
